examples.question_text:
A liquid has temperature $T=24+48e^{-0.2t}$, where $t\geq0$ is measured in minutes.
(a) Find its initial temperature.
(b) State its limiting temperature and whether it approaches this from above or below.
(c) Find its temperature after $5$ minutes, correct to one decimal place.
(d) Find when its temperature reaches $36^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$, correct to two decimal places.
examples.solution_text:
(a) Initially, $t=0$.
$\begin{aligned}T(0)&=24+48e^0\\&=72^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\end{aligned}$
(b) As $t\to\infty$, $e^{-0.2t}\to0$, so $T\to24^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. Since $48e^{-0.2t}>0$, the temperature approaches this limit from above. It never reaches the limit at a finite time.
$\begin{aligned}\text{(c)}\quad&T(5)&=24+48e^{-1}\\&&\approx41.7^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{(d)}\quad&36&=24+48e^{-0.2t}\\&12&=48e^{-0.2t}\\&e^{-0.2t}&=\frac14\\&-0.2t&=\ln\frac14\\&t&=\frac{\ln(1/4)}{-0.2}\\&&\approx6.93\end{aligned}$
The liquid reaches $36^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ after approximately $6.93$ minutes.

examples.question_text:
Water initially at $84^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ cools in a room held at $20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. Its rate of change of temperature is proportional to its temperature difference from the room. After $4$ minutes, its temperature is $68^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$.
(a) Find a model $T=20+Ae^{kt}$, keeping $k$ exact.
(b) Find its temperature after $12$ minutes.
(c) Find when it first comes within $1^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ of room temperature, correct to one decimal place.
examples.solution_text:
(a) Use $T=20+Ae^{kt}$.
$\begin{aligned}84&=20+A\\A&=64\end{aligned}$
At $t=4$:
$\begin{aligned}68&=20+64e^{4k}\\48&=64e^{4k}\\e^{4k}&=\frac34\\k&=\frac14\ln\frac34\end{aligned}$
Thus $T=20+64e^{kt}$, where $k=\frac14\ln\frac34<0$.
$\begin{aligned}\text{(b)}\quad&T(12)&=20+64e^{12k}\\&&=20+64\left(\frac34\right)^3\\&&=47^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\end{aligned}$
(c) The water cools towards $20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ from above. It first comes within $1^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ when $T=21^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$.
$\begin{aligned}21&=20+64e^{kt}\\1&=64e^{kt}\\e^{kt}&=\frac1{64}\\t&=\frac{\ln(1/64)}{k}\\&=\frac{4\ln(1/64)}{\ln(3/4)}\\&\approx57.8\end{aligned}$
It is within $1^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ of room temperature from approximately $57.8$ minutes onwards.

examples.question_text:
A bird population follows $N=6000+Ae^{kt}$, where $t$ is measured in years. Its long-run limiting population is $6000$. Initially there are $1000$ birds, and after $5$ years there are $2000$.
(a) Find $A$ and $k$ in exact form.
(b) Find the time threshold after which the population exceeds half its limiting population, correct to one decimal place.
examples.solution_text:
(a) At $t=0$:
$\begin{aligned}1000&=6000+A\\A&=-5000\end{aligned}$
At $t=5$:
$\begin{aligned}2000&=6000-5000e^{5k}\\-4000&=-5000e^{5k}\\e^{5k}&=\frac45\\k&=\frac15\ln\frac45\end{aligned}$
The model is $N=6000-5000e^{kt}$. Since $k<0$, the population increases towards $6000$ from below.
(b) Half the limiting population is $3000$. Solve for the threshold:
$\begin{aligned}3000&=6000-5000e^{kt}\\-3000&=-5000e^{kt}\\e^{kt}&=\frac35\\t&=\frac{\ln(3/5)}{k}\\&=\frac{5\ln(3/5)}{\ln(4/5)}\\&\approx11.4\end{aligned}$
The population equals $3000$ at the exact threshold $t=\frac{5\ln(3/5)}{\ln(4/5)}$ years and exceeds $3000$ afterwards. The threshold is approximately $11.4$ years.

examples.question_text:
A quantity satisfies $\frac{dQ}{dt}=k(Q-300)$. Initially $Q=200$, and when $t=4$, $Q=100$.
(a) Find its model in the form $Q=300+Ae^{kt}$.
(b) Find when the model predicts $Q=0$, correct to one decimal place.
(c) Sketch the model for $t\geq0$ and explain whether it has a finite limiting value.
